correctness.rationale: Cauchy–Binet equates squared normalized simplex determinants with the product Bernoulli covariance determinant. The exact integer 4368-subset determinant enumeration yields 480 and four times 64 weighted excess classes; reflection averaging gives 4e3(q)-18e4(q), checked with a standalone exact-integer program. A multi-affine nonnegative corner certificate proves the global sharp stability inequality and endpoint limits.

value.rationale: The independent but nonidentically distributed Bernoulli law is a natural four-parameter geometric-probability family attached directly to the first higher Hypercube inequality. An exact first/second determinant-moment ratio and sharp global bias-stability coefficient answer the natural optimization/classification question for the whole family. Not a recomputation of the fair endpoint alone.
